children.name: tls
children.description: Configure Transport Layer Security (TLS) settings to secure network connections. This includes options for standard TLS as well as mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication where both client and server authenticate each other using certificates. Key configuration options include `enabled` to enable TLS, `client_certs` for mTLS authentication, `root_cas`/`root_cas_file` for custom certificate authorities, and `skip_cert_verify` for development environments.

children.name: enabled
children.description: Whether to enable TLS for secure connections. Set to `true` to enable TLS encryption. Required to be `true` for other TLS options (like `client_certs`, `root_cas`, etc.) to take effect.

children.name: skip_cert_verify
children.description: Whether to skip server-side certificate verification. Set to `true` only for testing environments as this reduces security by disabling certificate validation. When using self-signed certificates or in development, this may be necessary, but should never be used in production. Consider using `root_cas` or `root_cas_file` to specify trusted certificates instead of disabling verification entirely.

children.name: sasl
children.description: Specify one or more methods or mechanisms of SASL authentication. They are tried in order. If the broker supports the first SASL mechanism, all connections use it. If the first mechanism fails, the client picks the first supported mechanism. If the broker does not support any client mechanisms, all connections fail.
children.short_description: One or more SASL authentication methods, tried in order until the broker supports one.

children.name: mechanism
children.description: The SASL mechanism to use for authentication.
annotated_options: AWS IAM based authentication as specified by the 'aws-msk-iam-auth' java library.

children.name: consumer_group
children.description:
An optional consumer group. When you specify this value:

- The partitions of any topics specified in the `topics` field are automatically distributed across consumers that share the consumer group.
- Partition offsets are automatically committed and resumed under this name.

Consumer groups are not supported when you specify explicit partitions to consume from in the `topics` field.
children.short_description: An optional consumer group to consume as. Partitions and offsets are managed automatically across the group.

processors.name: retry
processors.summary: Attempts to execute a series of child processors until success.
processors.footnotes:
== Batching

When messages are batched the child processors of a retry are executed for each individual message in isolation, performed serially by default but in parallel when the field <<parallel, `parallel`>> is set to `true`. This is an intentional limitation of the retry processor and is done in order to ensure that errors are correctly associated with a given input message. Otherwise, the archiving, expansion, grouping, filtering and so on of the child processors could obfuscate this relationship.

If the target behavior of your retried processors is "batch aware", in that you wish to perform some processing across the entire batch of messages and repeat it in the event of errors, you can use an xref:components:processors/archive.adoc[`archive` processor] to collapse the batch into an individual message. Then, within these child processors either perform your batch aware processing on the archive, or use an xref:components:processors/unarchive.adoc[`unarchive` processor] in order to expand the single message back out into a batch.

For example, if the retry processor were being used to wrap an HTTP request where the payload data is a batch archived into a JSON array it should look something like this:

```yaml
pipeline:
  processors:
    - archive:
        format: json_array
    - retry:
        processors:
          - http:
              url: example.com/nope
              verb: POST
    - unarchive:
        format: json_array
```

children.name: max_retries
children.description: The maximum number of retry attempts before the request is aborted. Setting this value to `0` will result in unbounded number of retries.

bloblang-functions.name: counter
bloblang-functions.description: Generates an incrementing sequence of integers starting from a minimum value (default 1). Each counter instance maintains its own independent state across message processing. When the maximum value is reached, the counter automatically resets to the minimum.

named.name: min
named.description: The starting value of the counter. This is the first value yielded. Evaluated once when the mapping is initialized.

named.name: max
named.description: The maximum value before the counter resets to min. Evaluated once when the mapping is initialized.

named.name: set
named.description: An optional query that controls counter behavior: when it resolves to a non-negative integer, the counter is set to that value; when it resolves to `null`, the counter is read without incrementing; when it resolves to a deletion, the counter resets to min; otherwise the counter increments normally.

examples.summary: Generate sequential IDs for each message.
Use a custom range for the counter.
Increment a counter multiple times within a single mapping using a named map.
Conditionally reset a counter based on input data.
Peek at the current counter value without incrementing by using null in the set parameter.

bloblang-functions.name: now
bloblang-functions.description: Returns the current timestamp as an RFC 3339 formatted string with nanosecond precision. Use this to add processing timestamps to messages or measure time between events. Chain with `ts_format` to customize the format or timezone.

examples.summary: Format the timestamp in a custom format and timezone.

bloblang-functions.name: uuid_v4
bloblang-functions.description: Generates a random RFC-4122 version 4 UUID. Use this for creating unique identifiers that don't reveal timing information or require ordering. Each invocation produces a new globally unique ID.

examples.summary: Add unique request IDs for tracing.
